privacy.charityManagementBody: Administrators and current level-6 stewards can review donations and see the donor’s site ID, Discord ID, display name, recorded source details and donation/review notes. Level-5 trainees can see necessary information and maintain charity settings only within their authorized mainstream-model scope, including eligible unbound mainstream candidates. Shared key settings can affect every model using that key. Managers do not receive configured key secrets; original provider-error diagnostics have the separate exception described above. New donations require a yes/no choice about manual Discord public thanks; submission makes that choice immutable. Old unconfirmed records are not permission for public thanks. Review records preserve the acting role and remove its account link on deletion. Public model settings are shared configuration, not a creator’s private export. Authorized discovery can refresh managed donation keys without showing their secrets. Failure thresholds default to 10; zero disables error-triggered removal only. Counts and ordinary expiry, withdrawal, manual switches and quotas retain their effect. The safe current threshold and owned-key limits are included in account export.
privacy.keyLimitsBody: The concurrency and RPM limits you set for a service key apply to both personal and charity model calls. Your account export includes these settings. Administrators and level-6 stewards can read them on resources they are authorized to manage, but cannot change them. The settings are deleted with the key.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy describes the data used to operate a NonbiriAPI instance.
privacy.notice: Deployment template: before accepting real users, the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, retention details and governing-law statements as required by the deployment and applicable law. This text is not legal advice.
privacy.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source software. Each deployed instance is operated independently by the person or organization that controls it. This policy applies to data processed by that operator, not to the public source repository or to Discord and third-party AI services acting under their own policies.
privacy.identityBody: The user station uses Discord for registration and sign-in. The service receives a Discord identifier, username, avatar information, and the membership information needed to check server and role eligibility. Sign-in tokens are used only during sign-in and are not stored as account data. The service keeps limited account, sign-in, and preference information and protects sign-in cookies according to the deployment configuration.
privacy.dataBody: The service stores your account profile, preferences, endpoints, encrypted service keys, discovered models, platform models, donations, usage, check-ins, activities and games. Some resource settings describe how to forward a request; they do not contain the request itself. An account API key is shown in full once, after which only verification and identification material remains. Account export version 10 contains your safe resources, four asset balances and financial history, game records and available randomness proofs, donation limits, activity exchanges, safe image-task outcomes and inactivity actions. It excludes full keys, encrypted key content, sign-in tokens, raw diagnostics, source IP and client clues, risk evidence, private administrator configuration, prompts, images, full execution parameters, internal upstream task identifiers, unrevealed game secrets and other users’ identities.
privacy.creditHistoryBody: You can filter your own credit history by asset. A mixed payment or activity exchange can appear as separate asset entries for the same operation. Entries related to your API calls can link to your request logs while those logs remain available. Donation rewards do not reveal another user's request ID or logs. Request-log expiry does not remove credit history.
privacy.economyBody: The service records separate general-credit and game-credit wallets, each of which may be negative. General check-ins, donation rewards and game winnings go to general credits. Game check-ins and daily welfare go to game credits. API calls, Thursday contributions and Thursday rewards use General Credits; insufficient General Credits do not cause a Game Credit debit. Game admission uses available game credits first and general credits for the remainder. Eligible refunds return the original assets; remaining stakes at a normal Rock Paper Scissors finish and game winnings use general credits. Each change records its asset and amount. The cumulative donor-reward total is a lifetime statistic used for donation summaries and level requirements, not spendable funds. No game result or economic return is guaranteed, and level 4 provides no game-economy advantage. Leaderboards are anonymous by default. Choosing a public profile shows your current server nickname or username and Discord avatar URL; no avatar copy or historical profile copy is stored. Draft paper and brushes are separate whole-unit activity assets; they are not game-payment funds and cannot be exchanged back to general/game credits or into each other.
privacy.credentialsBody: Configured service keys are not deliberately exposed through ordinary lists, alerts, caller errors, exports or URLs. An upstream may echo a credential into the restricted original-error diagnostics described below. The browser receives only the information needed to describe a key and does not save the full service key or account API key. Deleting a key or account immediately stops future calls through it. Encrypted key content that no longer belongs to any resource is cleared within one hour. An OpenAI-compatible key can ask the connected service not to store requests (store=false), but that service may ignore or reject the request. This is not a promise of zero retention and does not control the provider's abuse monitoring. Operators must still protect the server, complete backups, and master-key file.
privacy.trafficBody: Forwarded requests create limited records such as the account, model, service used, time, status, duration, and available token usage. Request bodies and successful response bodies are not actively logged; restricted original upstream errors follow the separate policy below. Debug starts in preview mode: it does not access a key, send a request outside the site, set aside charity credits, or record usage. Each real send requires separate confirmation and may use provider quota or charity credits. Debug request and response summaries with sensitive content removed exist only in the current process and page memory. They are not written to the database, ordinary logs, alerts, exports, backups, URLs, or browser storage, and are cleared when the session closes, is replaced, or expires, and on sign-out, restriction, account deletion, or service restart. Disconnecting the Debug page does not cancel an original request made with an account API key. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read and export the same limited request logs, including the caller’s site ID and actual charges. Details also show routing key identifiers for each attempt. Their charity logs also show the caller’s latest synced Discord name and ID. Deleted identity data is not restored. An active legal preservation requirement may allow these managers to read an older record by its ID; it does not extend ordinary lists or exports. Steward reads of these held records retain first and last access times and a count with the preservation record. Account deletion removes the steward identity from that audit. Chat and embedding inputs, including text and Token IDs, are processed for the requested operation. Returned vectors are used for the response only and are not saved in Debug or persistent records. Authenticated requests refused before the model handler may also record the safe refusal stage and reason, without an upstream attempt, Token usage or model-call fee. A separately configured abuse deduction remains a distinct financial operation.
privacy.sharingBody: Request content may be sent to OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible or native AI SDK Gateway v3 services selected by the account owner, including donor-provided charity resources operated by OpenAI, Anthropic, or another independent third party. A third party may process or retain request content, account logs, or abuse-monitoring data under its own policy, which the instance operator cannot control. A charity donor controls the related third-party account or key and may therefore see full request content in that service's account logs. Donating a key alone does not give access to caller identity or request content in this site's interface; authorized steward access is described separately. OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible requests also include a system-generated safety code that can be linked only for the same user, deployment, and third-party service. It hides direct identity but is not fully anonymous. Discord processes sign-in activity under its own policy. The operator may disclose data when required by law or needed to protect the service, users, or public safety, and must describe access by other data processors, hosting providers, and support staff. For OpenAI-compatible embeddings, this code replaces the request's user field; caller-supplied identity in that field is not forwarded. Native AI SDK Gateway v3 calls omit cost attribution by default. If the administrator enables it, chat and text embedding calls send a server-generated pseudonym scoped to the user and final gateway origin. The gateway can link requests in that scope for cost attribution. The label is not anonymous, contains no raw account or Discord ID, and does not mean that the gateway applies a safety identifier. Callers cannot override it. Debug shows only whether the label was sent, not its value.
privacy.retentionBody: Request logs are kept for up to 30 days. Recurring donation limits store rule settings, usage and in-flight reservations. Completed sliding-window usage totals are kept for at most 35 days; fixed periods keep the current period and any older period still needed to finish a call. Unfinished accounting keeps only the facts needed to settle it. These totals contain no request content or caller identity. Shared donation handling follows the donation's retention period; deleting its processing actor removes the account link without keeping a name or Discord copy. Records of completed donations and reviews, daily activity summaries, and completed charity payment holds are kept for 400 days. After a donated key ends or its service key is deleted, non-reversible information used only to match new abuse reports may remain for up to 90 days and cannot be used to make a call. The minimum target and donation-source relationship already saved for a report follows that case's own 90-day period or an active legal preservation requirement. Viewing a record does not extend these periods, and legal preservation does not extend the new-report matching period. Fishing, LinkLink and Rock Paper Scissors rounds, settlements, and shared results are kept for 30 days after settlement; a paid but unfinished round remains until settlement, and a private Rock Paper Scissors result remains until you acknowledge it or delete the account. LinkLink boards show each user's best completed score by size over 7 or 30 days, with earlier achievements first for equal scores. Fishing personal bests, asset-tagged credit changes, profile-visibility preferences, and the completion time and award for each once-only game newcomer task remain for the life of the account. Newcomer completion records are included in your export and deleted with your account. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read non-administrator account profiles, limits, levels, both wallets and usage. Stewards may modify only other current level-1–5 accounts and cannot delete accounts or change cumulative donor credit; they can also manage announcements and donated-key failure streaks. These actions retain audits without secrets. Announcement audits last 365 days with actor identity removed after 90 days; donation reviews follow the 400-day donation retention. Debug content is not stored long term. Sign-in sessions expire after inactivity or their maximum lifetime. Resolved administrator alerts are cleared after 30 days; unresolved alerts are subject to number limits and duplicate merging. Export version 10 allows up to 10,000 rows in each collection and 16 MiB for the complete JSON. An oversized export fails clearly and is not shortened. Account deletion invalidates sign-in sessions and account API keys, clears linked private data, and keeps only necessary facts without personal identity for the periods described above. Late callbacks cannot recreate the account. Complete operator backups and third-party services may retain copies under their own policies. Bidding Duel and Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) keep participant-accessible full match records for 30 days after settlement. After that, complete rule traces remain in an administrator-only anonymous archive without user references, original match or operation IDs, absolute times, payment sources or cross-match identity links. During a match, unused opposing equipment stays hidden; personal exports omit opposing identities and saved profile copies. Administrator batch export uses bounded pages and expiring signed continuation cursors. Blackjack's corresponding retention is described below. Blackjack stores waiting entries, the original funding of each stake, hands and actions, frozen terms, preset emotes and settlement facts. Participants and spectators can see current table seat labels, revealed cards, stakes, results and emotes, without account identities, wallet balances or other players' funding sources. Dealer hole cards and the undealt sequence are not provided to players during decisions. Participants and administrators can read game records for 30 days after settlement, followed by administrator-only anonymous long-term facts without account references, original game IDs, absolute times, funding sources or emotes. Waiting entries persist across rounds without a waiting timeout until seating, voluntary departure or removal under maintenance, game closure, ban or account-deletion rules. Account export version 10 includes safe personal queue and game records within the 10,000-row per-game and 16 MiB total bounds. Deletion detaches identity and auto-stands its hands without cancelling other players. The six games also store an independent random seed, opening commitment and bounded draw transcript for each game. Unrevealed seeds, future draws and hidden plans stay on the server and are not provided to players through state, logs or account exports. Before a multi-stage game ends, its proof provides only public information such as the commitment. Blackjack reveals its seed after the whole table finishes decisions and the result commits; Bidding Duel, Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test), Three-player Rock Paper Scissors and LinkLink reveal after the entire game ends. The presentation in each battle round does not end the match. Instantly settled Fishing batches provide proofs alongside results; cancelled games may reveal after the server commits cancellation. Participants can verify and download proofs, including safe proofs in account export version 10. Current Blackjack table spectators can read that table's public proof but do not gain participant history access. Proofs follow their parent records, with personal access lasting at most 30 days after completion; anonymous archives remove seeds, commitments and proofs. The Site cannot subsequently remove public material already downloaded or saved by others. Loan records retain the accepted terms, time, linked financial operation and actual balances until account deletion. Temporary newcomer qualifications are released when their game resolves or is cancelled; safe qualification metadata is included in the personal export. Game rankings keep net-spending contributions for seven days, positive Bidding and Blackjack profit contributions for 30 days, and necessary historical totals until deletion. Ranking preferences and cumulative charity achievement times follow the account. Charity visibility is separate from game visibility and defaults to anonymous; banned accounts stay on leaderboards anonymously without their avatar. Active automatic penalties remain available, ended penalties and direct deductions for 90 days; ordinary request links disappear after 30 days. Current violation windows survive service restarts and are trimmed to the configured window; deletion clears their stored and in-memory state. Personal exports contain safe penalty summaries and adjustments, not internal thresholds, counted events or management evidence. Administrators and current level-6 stewards can read the authorized penalty history, rule snapshots and bounded evidence; historical restrictions without that evidence are identified as such.
privacy.rightsBody: Subject to applicable law and the instance operator's process, you can update supported account settings, request an export and delete your account through the elevated self-service flow. Deletion is destructive. Contact the instance operator for access, correction, restriction or other privacy requests; the operator must publish the appropriate contact channel before production use.
privacy.securityBody: The service checks resource ownership, encrypts stored keys, prevents requests from reaching protected network locations or following dangerous redirects, limits resource use, and stops later work when a request is cancelled. Sensitive responses ask browsers and intermediate services not to cache them. The OpenAI-only “convert tool calls to text” experiment converts only complete real calls and results. It never runs tools or invents results and may affect normal tool workflows; Anthropic connections cannot use it. No system is completely secure. Do not place keys in notes, model names, URLs, tool data, issue reports, or support messages.
privacy.contactBody: The instance operator must publish a privacy contact, effective date and applicable jurisdiction in this page before production use. Material changes to data collection, sharing or retention should be announced and handled according to applicable law.
privacy.diagnosticsBody: We do not actively record request bodies or successful response bodies. For troubleshooting, we retain original upstream failures from personal and charity calls, retries, streaming error events, model discovery and image-activity operations. An upstream error can echo your input, prompt or a credential; that original content may be retained. Only current administrators and level-6 stewards may read it, even when a request belongs to another user. Ordinary retention is 30 days, with at most 1 MiB per error and an administrator-configurable total payload budget of 1 GiB by default. Truncation, unavailable bodies and capacity omissions are identified. At capacity, new bodies are omitted while safe summaries remain. An explicit legal preservation requirement can extend the approved records’ retention, and those bodies still count toward the budget. Ordinary caller errors remain sanitized.
privacy.sourcesBody: We also retain the effective source IP, its trust quality and a limited set of client clues: User-Agent, the originating site from Origin/Referer/HTTP-Referer, client titles and selected SDK language, version and runtime headers. URL paths, query strings and fragments are not retained in these origin fields. This information is bounded, normally retained for 30 days and visible only to administrators and level-6 stewards. It is not included in personal exports. Client headers are self-reported and can be absent, forged or changed by a relay; a shared IP can represent a household or shared network.
privacy.auditBody: Administrators and level-6 stewards may review sustained RPM or concurrency use, shared source addresses and manually maintained client clues for both personal and charity calls. Initial defaults flag at least 80% of the effective quota for five complete consecutive minutes, or at least three accounts using the same qualified IP within 24 hours. Review pages identify coverage gaps and supporting observations; a match does not prove misuse and these new findings do not automatically punish an account. Existing configured abuse rules continue independently. Selected model-list and compatibility-probe requests also contribute bounded access events: only valid account API keys link an event to an account and key generation, while unauthenticated requests contribute separate anonymous counts without an IP or client identity record. Key rotation, revocation and deletion remove key attribution. Administrators alone can inspect separate issuance, retirement, transfers and stock for each of the four assets; refunds and internal transfers are not treated as new issuance.
privacy.imageBody: Draft paper and brushes are separate whole-unit activity balances. Exchanges, reservations, charges and refunds have their own ledger records. The execution copy of image prompts and complete parameters stays only in server memory and is not actively written to request logs or the database. The configured independent provider receives them to generate the image. Valid image results stay only in server memory for a ten-minute pickup window and in the browser memory after loading; the service does not save images to disk, the database or successful-response logs. Closing the page, expiry or a service restart can lose a result. A successful task is not refunded for that loss. Safe task status, image counts and charging outcomes remain available for 30 days; financial records follow the ledger policy and safe facts are included in your export. Queue views show totals and your own position, not the identities of other participants. Raw provider failures follow the restricted diagnostic policy above.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: By using a NonbiriAPI instance, you agree to use it lawfully and protect your own credentials.
terms.notice: Deployment template: the instance operator must replace the operator identity, contact channel, effective date, governing law and complaint process before accepting real users. This text is not legal advice.
terms.operatorBody: NonbiriAPI is open-source gateway software, not an AI model provider. The operator of a particular instance controls its access rules, connected third-party services, limits, maintenance, and user support. The public source project and its copyright holder do not automatically operate every deployment.
terms.accessBody: An account may require Discord OAuth and membership of a configured server and role. You are responsible for activity performed through your account and must provide information that is accurate enough for the operator's access and support process. The operator may pause new registration or suspend access for security, maintenance, legal compliance or a breach of these terms.
terms.useBody: Use only endpoints, credentials and models that you are authorized to access. Do not use the service for unlawful activity, fraud, abuse, unauthorized access, credential theft, malware, harassment, privacy violations, sexual exploitation of minors, non-consensual intimate imagery, attacks against providers or other users, denial of service, rate-limit bypassing or attempts to defeat ownership and security controls.
terms.upstreamBody: Requests may be processed by OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic-compatible or native AI SDK Gateway v3 services selected by the account owner, including donor-provided charity resources. You must follow each service provider's terms, usage policies, licensing conditions, and content restrictions. A provider may keep request content, account logs, or abuse-monitoring data under its own policy. A request not to store content (store:false) may be ignored or rejected and is not a promise of zero retention. The operator does not guarantee that a third party will accept a request, preserve content, or keep an account available. Embedding calls require a compatible provider and model. Site chat-only request-storage and tool-conversion settings do not change embedding requests. A successful charity batch counts as one call; Token pricing uses all reported input tokens, and missing usage follows the displayed reserve rules. Native AI SDK Gateway v3 calls omit cost attribution by default. If the administrator enables it, chat and text embedding calls send a server-generated pseudonym scoped to the user and final gateway origin. The gateway can link requests in that scope for cost attribution. The label is not anonymous, contains no raw account or Discord ID, and does not mean that the gateway applies a safety identifier. Callers cannot override it. Debug shows only whether the label was sent, not its value.
terms.credentialsBody: Keep service keys, account API keys, sign-in links, and recovery information confidential. Replace a key immediately if it may have been exposed. Do not put keys in notes, URLs, model names, tools, issue reports, or support messages. You are responsible for submitted content and must have the right to send it to the selected provider. The experimental “convert tool calls to text” feature changes only how calls are displayed and sent. It does not run a tool, create a result, or prove success, and it may affect programs that expect structured tool calls.
terms.availabilityBody: Requests may be rate-limited, rejected, retried, or temporarily unavailable because of quotas, resource ownership, safety checks, third-party failures, maintenance, or permissions. A complete response is required for success; an HTTP status alone does not guarantee the result. Debug preview sends nothing outside the site, while a separately confirmed real send may consume provider quota or charity credits. Game prices, random results, recovery, and settlement are handled consistently by the game system and offer no guaranteed result or return. The operator may change limits or discontinue a prerelease service. Bidding Duel and Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) freeze their displayed entry price and fees when you queue. Game credits are spent first, then general credits. Queue cancellation, unmatched expiry, draws and system cancellations refund the original payment split. A decided match refunds the winner's entry and pays the loser's net entry as general credits after separately rounded fees. Surrender is a loss; disconnecting does not pause deadlines. A server restart, ban or deletion cancels an unfinished match. The battle presentation does not delay final accounting. Game points and resources do not have cash value. Blackjack starts at each server :00 and :30: 5 seconds for seating, 20 for simultaneous decisions and 5 for results. An early table finish may start results sooner, but the next game keeps its scheduled start. There is one table with up to nine seats; others may spectate. Up to 4,096 waiting players keep their first accepted FIFO position across rounds, unchanged by duplicate requests or refreshes. Waiters may leave at any time; seated players may leave before the 5-second deadline and be replaced in order. No replacements occur after that deadline. Once the whole game settles, participants must explicitly rejoin the tail, without reserved seats or automatic replay. Queue entry freezes terms and reserves the base stake using Game Credits first, then General Credits; changing the amount requires leaving and rejoining. Splits and doubles reserve additional stakes; insufficient funds reject the addition without changing the hand. Each hand's gross return pays separate platform, welfare and Thursday fees, defaulting to 1% each. All net returns, including pushes and principal, are General Credits; zero returns incur no extra fee. Under the defaults, a stake of 1,000 returns 0 for a loss, 970 for a push, 1,940 for an ordinary win and 2,425 for a natural blackjack. The game page shows full table rules, stake limits and fees. Long-term expected returns are negative, no individual outcome is guaranteed, and card order is not adjusted to a player's wins or losses. Waiting departures, exits within the seating window and system cancellations refund the actual original funding without fees. After dealing, disconnection, closing the page or timeout continues play with automatic standing and does not itself trigger a refund. Restart cancels the unsettled table while preserving unseated waiters and their reservations; committed results are never reversed. Maintenance or game closure refunds waiters and undealt seats while dealt tables finish. Banned dealt hands stand automatically. Deletion detaches identity while play finishes; unavailable proceeds go to the corresponding external asset account without recreating the account. The six games use independent cryptographically secure random seeds. You can save an opening commitment and verify or download the disclosed seed and draws after the server commits completion or cancellation of the whole game. Blackjack reveals during results after all table decisions end; Likes keeps its seed secret during intermediate round presentations. Instantly completed Fishing batches provide proofs only alongside results. Verification reproduces recorded draws and checks the seed against the original commitment; older games without proofs cannot be retroactively verified. Commitments do not guarantee returns and alone cannot prove the operator never preselected a seed. Game pages describe rules, public actions and verification. Each donated key has a consecutive-failure disable threshold, default 10, editable by its donor, an administrator or a current steward, including permitted steward automation. Saving retains the count and immediately recalculates error-disablement. Zero never disables for errors, although errors are still counted and success clears the count. Pages warn persistently without an extra confirmation. Manual disabling, expiry, withdrawal, bans and quotas still apply. The current threshold is included in safe account exports; policy audit records contain no key secrets and follow donation-review retention. When the optional loan activity is enabled, confirmation immediately adds the displayed game credits and deducts the displayed repayment from general credits, including the disclosed fee and interest. These are site credits, not a cash loan. A nonnegative general balance is required before borrowing, but repayment can make it negative; later general-credit income reduces that negative balance. Game credits remain usable. Each quote expires after 60 seconds or a configuration change and must be refreshed and confirmed again. The accepted record shows actual balances; displayed estimates can change before confirmation. Loan activity does not earn donor credit or count toward game rankings. Newcomer tasks pay once per account after eligible normal play, may stack in one result, and do not award for local teaching or system cancellation. Game leaderboards follow the stated net-spending or positive-profit calculation and exclude loans and newcomer awards. Optional sound and reduced-motion settings change presentation only; results and financial settlement remain server-controlled. New donation submissions and pending edits require a meaningful nonblank description.
terms.dataBody: The privacy policy describes information stored by the service, Debug handling, exports, and account deletion. After identity verification, deleting an account removes linked donation, charity, check-in, credit-change, and game data. The service opens only a structurally complete database that passes validation; an unrecognized, damaged, or incompatible database is rejected. A separately confirmed clean deployment first creates and verifies a complete snapshot, then removes the current database—including accounts, business data, site settings, and custom legal text—and starts with an empty database. A protected operator backup may retain the database, program, environment, and master key for recovery. The new environment must remain in maintenance with registration, activities, charity access, donation intake, and games closed until legal text, required settings, and initial data have been reapplied and checked. Backup recovery and third-party data retention follow the operator's and provider's respective policies. Bidding Duel, Turn-based Battle Minigame (Test) and Blackjack remove participant identity links; de-identified rule traces may remain long term as described in the Privacy Policy. Dealt Blackjack games continue automatic settlement without restoring the deleted account. Random proofs follow the Privacy Policy's cleanup periods and do not enter anonymous long-term archives.
terms.suspensionBody: The operator may suspend or terminate access when reasonably necessary to protect the service or users, comply with law or investigate a suspected breach. Where safe and lawful, the operator may provide notice. You may stop using the service and request account deletion through the supported flow.
terms.liabilityBody: To the extent permitted by applicable law, the service is provided as-is and as available, without a promise of uninterrupted operation, that every request reaches the expected service, model accuracy, data availability, or fitness for a particular purpose. The operator is not responsible for third-party provider decisions or content generated by third-party systems. Nothing in these terms excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

NonbiriAPI, Discord, OpenAI, and other names may be trademarks of their respective owners; this project is not automatically affiliated with or endorsed by third-party providers. Rights in submitted or generated content depend on your rights, applicable law, and third-party service terms.
terms.changesBody: The operator may update these terms for a new release or operational change. Material changes should state an effective date and be communicated as required by applicable law. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance where legally valid; otherwise stop using the service and contact the operator. The operator must publish a contact channel and governing-law statement before production use.
terms.donationBody: A new donation requires an explicit choice about allowing an administrator or level-6 steward to thank you manually in a Discord public channel. You cannot change that choice after submission; older unconfirmed records do not authorize public thanks. Charity calls cannot use your own donated keys unless you are currently a level-6 steward; personal models remain available under their normal rules. Exempt calls retain ordinary donor rewards. Donation limits may independently restrict total, input and output Tokens, and shared key changes affect all bindings. Charity-model forwarding can remove the configured optional top-level parameters. A recent success percentage describes the displayed observation window and sample, not a promise that your next request will succeed.
terms.imageBody: Limited activities need a configured opening period. Hiding an activity removes its directory entry but does not block an otherwise eligible visitor with its link. Reopening keeps balances and history. The picture-book activity exchanges general credits for draft paper and brushes; it does not support reverse exchange or exchange between those currencies. The default prices are 1,000 general credits per draft paper and 10,000 per brush. Brush supply is a cumulative shared cap, initially ten; reducing the cap does not confiscate existing balances, and task refunds do not restore exchange supply. Administrators may change future prices and settings. Submitting a task reserves both displayed currency amounts, multiplied by the requested image count, under the accepted model revision. Any valid partial success charges the full accepted task price. Failure, an unresolved result at the execution deadline, or cancellation before dispatch refunds both currencies. After dispatch you cannot cancel, and closing the page does not cancel. The server controls ordering and upstream requests; no participant receives a privileged queue or free allowance. Default queue and execution limits are 30 minutes each. Successful images have a ten-minute memory pickup window and may be lost on page closure, expiry or restart without a refund. Restart refunds queued tasks whose in-memory payload was lost; an uncertain upstream submission is never automatically repeated. Natural activity end lets accepted work finish, while manual pause or maintenance cancels undispatched tasks and refunds them. Bans prevent result access; account deletion removes private data while minimal anonymous execution cleanup may continue.
terms.inactivityBody: An administrator may enable an inactivity policy; it is disabled by default. The user site displays the applicable rules and expected processing dates. Successful login or API use, check-ins, benefit claims and effective game/activity actions count as activity; passive rewards and background polling do not. Administrators and levels 5 and 6 are exempt, but owning a usable donated key does not create an exemption. Configured decay affects only positive available general/game balances, with separate rates or fixed amounts, periods and retained floors. It does not take frozen funds or activity currencies or deepen a negative balance. First enablement, re-enablement and stricter rules grant at least seven days. A missed series of decay periods is caught up at most once; if protective banning is due at the same check, banning takes priority without decay. A protective permanent ban preserves the account and balances, stops future decay, and can be reversed by an administrator, restarting observation. Existing donations remain usable and earn normal rewards only for this protective ban reason; the banned account still cannot log in or call APIs.
